reasoning: Proper colorings of C_n with k colors = (k-1)^n + (-1)^n (k-1). For n=7: (k-1)^7 - (k-1). Choose which 3 of the 4 palette colors are used: C(4,3)=4 ways. For a fixed set of 3 colors, count surjective proper colorings by inclusion-exclusion: P(C7,3) - C(3,2)·P(C7,2) + C(3,1)·P(C7,1). P(C7,3)=2^7-2=126; P(C7,2)=1^7-1=0 (odd cycle is not 2-colorable); P(C7,1)=0. So surjective count with exactly 3 given colors = 126 - 0 + 0 = 126. Total = 4 × 126 = 504. (Check: total proper 4-colorings = 3^7-3 = 2184; exactly-2 = 0, exactly-1 = 0, so exactly-4 = 2184 - 504 = 1680.)
prompt:
The vertices of a 7-cycle are colored with colors from a palette of 4 colors so that adjacent vertices get different colors. How many such colorings use exactly 3 of the 4 colors? Vertices are labeled, so rotations and reflections count as different colorings.

Give the final answer as a single integer, and nothing else, in the answer field. In the reasoning field, lay out the cases you split on and the count for each case.
